1	# Epic 6 Context: Conversational Memory, Save-to-Journal & Insights
2	
3	<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	Users hold a persistent, multi-session conversation with an assistant whose answers are grounded in semantic retrieval over their own past Entries — not generic replies — can turn their own reflective chat messages into real journal Entries with one tap, and occasionally receive an unprompted insight about a pattern in their own writing. None of this (dropped streams, save failures, insight-generation failures) may ever block, corrupt, or freeze the core chat experience. This epic is the product's central differentiator: proving the memory-over-own-history bet end-to-end against the real backend.
8	
9	## Stories
10	
11	- Story 6.1: Send Message & Receive RAG-Grounded Streaming Response
12	- Story 6.2: Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation
13	- Story 6.3: Dropped-Stream Resilience & Offline Composer Lock
14	- Story 6.4: Bookmark a Chat Message into an Entry
15	- Story 6.5: Proactive Insight Injection & Failure Isolation
16	
17	## Requirements & Constraints
18	
19	- Chat responses stream via SSE and must be grounded in retrieval over the user's own Entries; exactly three visible states exist for a response: streaming/processing, error, complete — no others.
20	- A Chat Message never auto-creates an Entry; saving one to the journal (this epic's story 6.4) is the sole explicit exception.
21	- A user holds multiple named Chat Sessions, switchable and startable from the side menu; starting a new session requires connectivity (blocked offline, consistent with the offline composer lock). A returning session restores its last scroll position.
22	- A dropped response stream keeps the partial message on screen with a failure indicator (never clears bubble content) and is recoverable via a dedicated retry call that regenerates without duplicating the original question.
23	- Offline disables the message composer (and the new-session entry point) with an offline banner, while existing history remains fully visible/scrollable.
24	- The save-to-journal (bookmark) affordance appears only on the user's own messages, never on AI responses; it creates an Entry carrying a reference back to the source chat message, through the same shared entries-feature use case introduced earlier in delivery — never by importing the entries repository/data source directly.
25	- Saving the same message twice is idempotent: no duplicate Entry, no conflict surfaced to the user (success, not error).
26	- A save failure never freezes the chat session or the button — the button returns to a retryable state and the rest of the session stays usable.
27	- An Insight is injected into the active session on exactly one trigger per satisfied window — either N user messages sent or a fixed inactivity timeout, whichever comes first — never both, never twice for the same window.
28	- An Insight-generation failure is silent to the user: no error overlay, composer stays enabled, ordinary chat keeps working. Insight quality/content is explicitly outside acceptance scope — only the trigger/injection/failure-isolation mechanism is graded.
29	- Dismissing an Insight never affects scroll position or any other conversation state.
30	
31	## Technical Decisions
32	
33	- Feature lives at `features/chat/`; it consumes `features/entries/`'s abstract save/create-entry port from `entries/domain` only — never anything from `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/` (layering invariant, zero violations tolerated).
34	- Repositories return `Future<Either<Failure, T>>`, except the chat response itself, which is `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` given its SSE nature. The closed, 14-member `Failure` hierarchy (13 server codes + a local-only malformed-response code) is shared from `core/` and never redefined per feature.
35	- Chat holds no local write queue: a send attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to a `networkOffline` failure, never queued. Plain history reads (sessions, messages) transparently fall back to the local cache; retry logic for retryable failure codes lives once in the shared API client, not reimplemented per feature.
36	- Chat's message/streaming state is its own sealed state class (append-only, streaming-aware) — explicitly excluded from the shared generic `Resource<T>` single-fetch state pattern, because it isn't a single fetch.
37	- The proactive-insight overlay is a value appended onto the existing chat state from story 6.1, never a second parallel state container.
38	- A never-throws `core/isolated_side_effect.dart` helper (`Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped) ships with this epic's first consumer (the save-to-journal story) and is reused unawaited (fire-and-forget) by the insight story so a slow/failed insight never blocks or delays the chat stream.
39	- No BLoC/Cubit ever takes another BLoC/Cubit as a constructor dependency, in this feature or across features; independent state sources compose via injected domain streams/use-cases or `BlocListener`, never a direct BLoC-to-BLoC reference.
40	- The entries-owning feature's save port is idempotent on the save-to-journal identifier at the implementation level (not just the type signature) — a repeat save for the same source message never creates a second Entry.
41	- Session/message/sync-badge local caching follows the same per-feature local-cache-box convention used by other features; cursor-based pagination for session and message lists follows the server's own cursor convention verbatim.
42	
43	## UX & Interaction Patterns
44	
45	- Chat bubbles: user (sage, squared bottom-right corner) vs. AI (ivory, squared bottom-left, resting elevation). A streaming AI bubble adds a blinking cursor at the text's end and nothing else changes visually while generating; under Reduce Motion the cursor blink is skipped and final text shows immediately instead.
46	- A dropped/failed response replaces the bubble's timestamp slot with red retry copy; bubble text itself is never cleared.
47	- Bookmark button: four states on every user message only — idle (outline) / saving (spinner, or a static label under Reduce Motion) / saved (ochre check) / error (red warning). Tapping an already-saved message is a no-op. State must be carried by icon + color together, never color alone. Tap target ≥44pt.
48	- Insight card: ochre left spine, mono "INSIGHT" label, dismiss "x" — the spine is the only accent-colored element inside the chat stream itself.
49	- Offline banner disables sending only; conversation history stays scrollable and readable underneath it. A session-expired overlay (re-auth) can appear over chat without losing scroll position or in-memory history.
50	- A new session opens with the composer focused and only the placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem..." — no invented greeting copy.
51	- No swipe gestures, no nested overlays, no pull-to-refresh beyond what the session/message endpoints already govern.
52	
53	## Cross-Story Dependencies
54	
55	- Story 6.1 establishes the chat stream/state machine that 6.2 (sessions), 6.3 (retry/offline), 6.4 (bookmark), and 6.5 (insight overlay) all build on or append to.
56	- Story 6.4 is this epic's (and the codebase's) first consumer of the shared `isolated_side_effect` helper; Story 6.5 reuses that same helper fire-and-forget.
57	- Story 6.4 depends on the entries feature's save/create-entry port already existing from earlier delivery work; it must not introduce a second entry model or reach into entries' data layer.
58	- Story 6.5's insight overlay is layered onto 6.1's chat state rather than a separate state container, so it cannot be built independently of 6.1's state shape.

1	import '../../../../core/failure/failure.dart';
2	import '../../domain/entities/chat_message.dart';
3	
4	/// `ChatCubit`'s own sealed state — AD-12: "Chat's state is its own sealed
5	/// class, never forced into `Resource<T>`", because it isn't a single
6	/// fetch (the append-only [ChatReady.messages] list keeps growing one
7	/// token at a time while a response streams in, long after the initial
8	/// bootstrap fetch that produced it has already resolved).
9	sealed class ChatState {
10	  const ChatState();
11	}
12	
13	/// The initial state, and the state while `ChatCubit.init()`'s own
14	/// session-bootstrap (list-or-create-one-session) + history fetch are
15	/// still in flight.
16	class ChatBootstrapLoading extends ChatState {
17	  const ChatBootstrapLoading();
18	}
19	
20	/// I/O matrix: "Bootstrap failure" — `chat-sessions-list`/`create` (or the
21	/// history fetch right after) failed; the screen shows this generic error
22	/// state instead of spinning forever.
23	class ChatBootstrapError extends ChatState {
24	  const ChatBootstrapError(this.failure);
25	
26	  final Failure failure;
27	
28	  @override
29	  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
30	      identical(this, other) ||
31	      (other is ChatBootstrapError && other.failure == failure);
32	
33	  @override
34	  int get hashCode => failure.hashCode;
35	}
36	
37	/// The composer is enabled, [messages] renders — [ChatUiMessage]'s own
38	/// [ChatUiMessage.status] drives each bubble's one of the 3 visible states
39	/// (streaming/failed/complete, RF04's Acceptance Criteria).
40	class ChatReady extends ChatState {
41	  const ChatReady({
42	    required this.sessionId,
43	    required this.messages,
44	    this.isSending = false,
45	  });
46	
47	  final String sessionId;
48	
49	  /// Append-only for the lifetime of this cubit (Code Map) — a message is
50	  /// ever only added to the end, or mutated in place by id (a streaming
51	  /// AI bubble's own `content`/`status`), never removed or reordered.
52	  final List<ChatUiMessage> messages;
53	
54	  /// Whether `ChatCubit.sendMessage`'s own send is actively in flight —
55	  /// the composer's one enable/disable signal (`_ChatComposer`). Kept as
56	  /// its own field rather than derived by scanning [messages] for a
57	  /// persisted `streaming` status: a message restored from history/cache
58	  /// can legitimately carry that status without a send being in flight
59	  /// (I/O matrix: mid-stream drop), which would otherwise permanently
60	  /// disable the composer.
61	  final bool isSending;
62	
63	  ChatReady copyWith({List<ChatUiMessage>? messages, bool? isSending}) =>
64	      ChatReady(
65	        sessionId: sessionId,
66	        messages: messages ?? this.messages,
67	        isSending: isSending ?? this.isSending,
68	      );
69	}
70	
71	/// One bubble's own presentation-layer shape — distinct from the domain
72	/// `ChatMessage` entity (Code Map) because a message in flight has no
73	/// server-assigned `seq`/`retryCount`/`createdAt` yet; [id] is a locally
74	/// generated, UI-only identifier (`ChatCubit._nextLocalId()`), never the
75	/// server's own message id (Design Notes: `message_created`'s id is the
76	/// *user* message's server id, unused by this story — see
77	/// `ChatStreamEvent`'s own doc).
78	class ChatUiMessage {
79	  const ChatUiMessage({
80	    required this.id,
81	    required this.role,
82	    required this.content,
83	    required this.status,
84	  });
85	
86	  final String id;
87	  final ChatMessageRole role;
88	  final String content;
89	  final ChatMessageStatus status;
90	
91	  ChatUiMessage copyWith({String? content, ChatMessageStatus? status}) =>
92	      ChatUiMessage(
93	        id: id,
94	        role: role,
95	        content: content ?? this.content,
96	        status: status ?? this.status,
97	      );
98	
99	  @override
100	  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
101	      identical(this, other) ||
102	      (other is ChatUiMessage &&
103	          other.id == id &&
104	          other.role == role &&
105	          other.content == content &&
106	          other.status == status);
107	
108	  @override
109	  int get hashCode => Object.hash(id, role, content, status);
110	
111	  @override
112	  String toString() =>
113	      'ChatUiMessage(id: $id, role: $role, content: $content, '
114	      'status: $status)';
115	}

8	/// Tela 3 — Menu lateral, the sole navigation hub (Boundaries: "no
9	/// drawer-within-drawer, no tab bar"). Native Flutter `Drawer` (Boundaries:
10	/// "not a hand-rolled overlay like `ConfirmationDialog`").
11	///
12	/// The header shows a generic, non-personalized [Avatar] + static label —
13	/// no real logged-in identity is wired up yet (Boundaries; see
14	/// deferred-work.md for why). There is no `CONVERSAS`/past-session list
15	/// (RF04/RF07 aren't built) — only the static "Novo Chat" action (closes
16	/// the drawer, no-op) and the three nav items.
17	class AppDrawer extends StatefulWidget {
18	  const AppDrawer({super.key});
19	
20	  @override
21	  State<AppDrawer> createState() => _AppDrawerState();
22	}
23	
24	class _AppDrawerState extends State<AppDrawer> {
25	  // Guards every action below against a rapid double-tap (on the same
26	  // item, or a different one) firing `Navigator.of(context).pop()` twice —
27	  // the second call would land after the drawer's own pop already started
28	  // closing it, popping the route beneath the drawer instead of being a
29	  // no-op (code review, Story 1.6).
30	  bool _actionTaken = false;
31	
32	  @override
33	  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
34	    return Drawer(
35	      width: DesignTokens.drawerWidth,
36	      backgroundColor: DesignTokens.colorSurfaceElevated,
37	      shape: const RoundedRectangleBorder(),
38	      // No `SafeArea` here — `drawerContentPadding`'s fixed top value (59)
39	      // already clears the status bar, same convention every other header
40	      // in this story uses (`ChatScreen`'s own header, `_BackArrowHeader`
41	      // in `placeholder_screens.dart`); the epic's fixed 390x844 single
42	      // frame has no responsive/dynamic-inset handling anywhere else, so
43	      // stacking `SafeArea` on top would double-count that clearance.
44	      child: Padding(
45	        padding: DesignTokens.drawerContentPadding,
46	        child: Column(
47	          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
48	          children: [
49	            Container(
50	              padding: DesignTokens.drawerHeaderPadding,
51	              decoration: const BoxDecoration(
52	                border: Border(
53	                  bottom: BorderSide(color: DesignTokens.colorBorder),
54	                ),
55	              ),
56	              child: const Row(
57	                children: [
58	                  Avatar(initials: 'U'),
59	                  SizedBox(width: DesignTokens.drawerHeaderGap),
60	                  Text('Usuário', style: DesignTokens.textTitleSm),
61	                ],
62	              ),
63	            ),
64	            const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.spacingMd),
65	            _DrawerPrimaryAction(
66	              icon: Icons.add,
67	              label: 'Novo Chat',
68	              // No real chat yet (RF04/RF07) — closes the drawer, stays
69	              // on `/` (I/O matrix: "drawer closes, stays on /").
70	              onTap: () => _closeDrawer(context),
71	            ),
72	            const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.spacingSm),
73	            // Second drawer block (code review, Story 1.6): the prototype's
74	            // own markup groups "Novo Chat" separately from the three
75	            // static nav items below, via a `border-top` + `padding-top`
76	            // on this section (ground truth: `cerne-prototype.html`'s
77	            // `<!-- OVERLAY: Drawer -->` block) — not reproduced until now.
78	            Container(
79	              padding: DesignTokens.drawerSectionDividerPadding,
80	              decoration: const BoxDecoration(
81	                border: Border(
82	                  top: BorderSide(color: DesignTokens.colorBorder),
83	                ),
84	              ),
85	              child: Column(
86	                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
87	                children: [
88	                  _DrawerNavItem(
89	                    icon: Icons.menu_book_outlined,
90	                    label: 'Meus Registros',
91	                    onTap: () =>
92	                        _navigate(context, AppRoutePaths.meusRegistros),
93	                  ),
94	                  _DrawerNavItem(
95	                    icon: Icons.view_kanban_outlined,
96	                    label: 'Planos de Ação',
97	                    onTap: () =>
98	                        _navigate(context, AppRoutePaths.planosDeAcao),
99	                  ),
100	                  _DrawerNavItem(
101	                    icon: Icons.settings_outlined,
102	                    label: 'Configurações',
103	                    onTap: () =>
104	                        _navigate(context, AppRoutePaths.configuracoes),
105	                  ),
106	                ],
107	              ),
108	            ),
109	          ],
110	        ),
111	      ),
112	    );
113	  }
114	
115	  void _closeDrawer(BuildContext context) {
116	    if (_actionTaken) {
117	      return;
118	    }
119	    _actionTaken = true;
120	    Navigator.of(context).pop();
121	  }
122	
123	  void _navigate(BuildContext context, String location) {
124	    if (_actionTaken) {
125	      return;
126	    }
127	    _actionTaken = true;
128	    Navigator.of(context).pop();
129	    context.go(location);
130	  }
131	}

59	  /// Only jumps to the bottom when the view was already there (or close
60	  /// to it) *before* this update, or hasn't attached to a scrollable yet
61	  /// (the very first history render) — otherwise a user who deliberately
62	  /// scrolled up to reread earlier history would get yanked back down on
63	  /// every single streamed token.
64	  void _scrollToBottomSoon() {
65	    if (_scrollController.hasClients) {
66	      final position = _scrollController.position;
67	      const nearBottomThreshold = 80.0;
68	      final wasNearBottom =
69	          position.maxScrollExtent - position.pixels <= nearBottomThreshold;
70	      if (!wasNearBottom) {
71	        return;
72	      }
73	    }
74	    WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback((_) {
75	      if (_scrollController.hasClients) {
76	        _scrollController.jumpTo(_scrollController.position.maxScrollExtent);
77	      }
78	    });
79	  }

8	/// The chat feature's one port — `features/chat/presentation` depends on
9	/// this abstract class only, never `chat/data` (RNF06). Every method but
10	/// [sendMessage] returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (RNF09); [sendMessage]
11	/// alone returns a `Stream` given the SSE nature of its response
12	/// (Boundaries).
13	abstract class ChatRepository {
14	  /// Calls `chat-sessions-list` (`ApiClient.get`, via
15	  /// `ChatRemoteDataSource`) — works offline via the `chat_sessions` Hive
16	  /// box (Code Map): on [Failure.networkOffline]/[Failure.networkTimeout],
17	  /// falls back to a full dump of that box, same "cache fallback"
18	  /// convention `EntriesRepositoryImpl.list()` already uses for its own
19	  /// first/fresh page. Every other [Failure] propagates as `Left`,
20	  /// unmapped (RNF09).
21	  Future<Either<Failure, List<ChatSession>>> listSessions();
22	
23	  /// Calls `chat-sessions-create` (`ApiClient.post`) with no title
24	  /// (Boundaries: "`chat-sessions-create` with no title") — blocked
25	  /// offline per `requirements.md` ("`POST /chat/sessions` — blocked
26	  /// offline"), so unlike [listSessions] there is no cache fallback here:
27	  /// every [Failure], including [Failure.networkOffline], is returned as
28	  /// `Left`, unmapped. On success, persists the new session to the
29	  /// `chat_sessions` Hive box before returning `Right`, same
30	  /// "persist then return" ordering [listSessions] already uses.
31	  Future<Either<Failure, ChatSession>> createSession();
32	
33	  /// Calls `chat-messages-list` (`ApiClient.get`, [sessionId] appended as
34	  /// the one trailing path segment) — works offline via the
35	  /// `chat_messages` Hive box, same cache-fallback convention
36	  /// [listSessions] already uses, filtered to [sessionId] and sorted by
37	  /// `seq` ascending (the backend's own "ordered by seq", `openapi.yaml`).
38	  Future<Either<Failure, List<ChatMessage>>> listMessages(String sessionId);
39	
40	  /// Calls `chat-messages-send` (`ApiClient.postStream`, [sessionId]
41	  /// appended as the one trailing path segment) with `{content}` — the
42	  /// one streaming exception to this port's otherwise all-`Future` shape
43	  /// (Boundaries/RNF09: "every other method returns
44	  /// `Future<Either<Failure, T>>`"). No connectivity resolves immediately
45	  /// to a single `Left(Failure.networkOffline)` emission, never queued
46	  /// (Boundaries) — `ApiClient.postStream`'s own first awaited `Dio.post`
47	  /// call surfaces that failure before any byte streams. A connection that
48	  /// closes without a `done`/`error` SSE event is surfaced as a single
49	  /// trailing `Left(Failure.networkTimeout)` (Design Notes: "the taxonomy
50	  /// has no dedicated 'dropped stream' code"). No local write queue, no
51	  /// Hive persistence of sent messages (Design Notes: chat holds no local
52	  /// write queue for this story).
53	  Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>> sendMessage(
54	    String sessionId,
55	    String content,
56	  );
57	}

39	      identical(this, other) ||
40	      (other is ChatSession &&
41	          other.id == id &&
42	          other.title == title &&
43	          other.persona == persona &&
44	          other.userMessageCount == userMessageCount &&

62	      'ChatSession(id: $id, title: $title, persona: $persona, '

64	      'lastUserMessageAt: $lastUserMessageAt, createdAt: $createdAt, '
65	      'updatedAt: $updatedAt)';

1	# Cerne — Prototype extract
2	
3	The visual reference of the product is `cerne-prototype.html` (this folder). Open it in a browser; it needs JavaScript. This extract lists its navigable states, its visual tokens, its components and the implementation notes that come with it.
4	
5	- **Frame:** 390 × 844 logical points, portrait only, 4 dp grid.
6	- **Language of the interface:** Portuguese. Every UI text below appears exactly as in the prototype, in quotes.
7	- **Precedence:** the prototype defines appearance and states. Behavior rules (triggers, timings, filters, error handling) are defined in `docs/input/requirements.md`; where the prototype's simulated behavior differs from a requirement, the requirement prevails.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Navigation map
12	
13	The prototype has **32 navigable states**, reachable from a single state machine (a `screen` variable plus overlay flags). Not every state is a new full screen — several are **overlays** (modal, sheet, bottom sheet, dialog) shown on top of one of three base screens: **Home/Chat**, **Meus Registros** and **Configurações**. Overlays preserve the screen underneath (it stays visible, with a darkened scrim behind).
14	
15	```
16	Splash (auto, 1.8 s)
17	  └─> Biometria ──tap/error──> PIN inicial / PIN após falha
18	  │      └─> "usar e-mail e senha" ──> Entrar / criar conta (toggle)
19	  │                                          └─> submit ──> Home/Chat
20	  └─(PIN complete, 4 digits)──> Home/Chat
21	  └─(Face ID/Touch ID ok)──> Home/Chat
22	
23	Home/Chat (base screen)
24	  ├─ overlay: Sessão expirada (backend session expires; "Entrar novamente" ──> Biometria)
25	  ├─ overlay: side menu (☰ icon) ──> Meus Registros | Planos de Ação | Configurações | new conversation
26	  └─ overlay: Insertion modal ("+" button) ──> tabs Texto / Áudio / Foto, each with its own sub-states
27	        (on save, the modal closes and returns to Home/Chat with the record added)
28	
29	Meus Registros (base screen, from the side menu)
30	  ├─ empty state (no records) ──CTA "Criar primeiro registro"──> Insertion modal
31	  ├─ overlay: filter sheet ──"Aplicar"──> active filters (chips on the list)
32	  └─ overlay: export card (download icon) ──> pending ──> processing ──> done | error | empty period
33	
34	Planos de Ação (base screen, from the side menu) — static screen, 3-column kanban (extension, not implemented)
35	
36	Configurações (base screen, from the side menu)
37	  ├─ dashboard variations: zero entries | one entry | more than 30 (with narrative) | narrative unavailable
38	  ├─ inline profile-name editing
39	  ├─ AI persona selection (Analítico / Empático / Socrático) (extension, not implemented)
40	  ├─ "Sair" ──> Biometria
41	  └─ overlay: account-deletion confirmation ──"Apagar tudo"──> Biometria (same destination as logout)
42	```

The prototype's own state catalog has 32 entries: Tela 0 — Splash; Tela 0.1 — Biometria; Tela 0.1a — Entrar / criar conta; Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial; Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha; Tela 1 — Home / Chat; Tela 2 — Texto, Áudio (Gravando, Processando, Transcrito, Erro), Foto (Captura, Processando OCR, Reconhecido, Erro); Tela 3 — Menu lateral; Tela 1 — Sessão expirada; Tela 4 — Meus Registros, Estado vazio, Sheet de filtro, Filtros ativos; Exportar — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio; Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]**; Tela 6 — Configurações, Dashboard zero entradas, Dashboard uma entrada, Narrativa indisponível, Confirmar exclusão. The tables below group them by screen; some rows describe variations inside one state (e.g., the bookmark sub-states, the streaming response). input.message:
Implemented spec-6-2 (Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation) in full. Summary of changes, verification, and two deliberate deviations below.

## Files changed

- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart` — `ChatReady` gained `sessions: List<ChatSession>` and `restoreScrollOffset: double?`; `copyWith` extended to carry both.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart`
  - `_bootstrap()` now captures the resolved session list (including a freshly created one) into the emitted `ChatReady.sessions`.
  - Added `final Map<String, double> _scrollOffsets = {}` (in-memory, keyed by sessionId, lives on the long-lived cubit — never Hive, never ChatReady).
  - Added `recordScrollOffset(sessionId, offset)`.
  - Added `switchSession(sessionId) -> Future<Either<Failure, Unit>>`: no-op `Right` if already active; otherwise fetches history via the existing `listMessages`, emits a new `ChatReady` carrying whatever `_scrollOffsets[sessionId]` holds (or `null`).
  - Added `startNewSession() -> Future<Either<Failure, Unit>>`: calls existing `createSession()`; on `Left` (including offline) nothing is emitted at all — current session untouched; on success, new empty session becomes active, prepended to `sessions`.
- `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart` — rewritten to read `context.read<ChatCubit>()`/`BlocBuilder<ChatCubit, ChatState>` (the instance `ChatScreen` already provides via `BlocProvider<ChatCubit>.value`, never a second `sl<ChatCubit>()`). Added a "CONVERSAS" section (`_ConversasSection`/`_DrawerSessionItem`, reusing `drawerNavItemPadding`/`textBodyMd`/`textMonoCaption`/`spacingXs`/`spacingSm` — no new design tokens) listing every session title+timestamp, sorted most-recent-first, empty title falling back to "Nova conversa". Wired "Novo Chat" to `startNewSession()` and each row to `switchSession()`, both `await`ed with the `Left` surfaced as a `ScaffoldMessenger` `SnackBar` (`failure.message` verbatim, same convention `TextEntryError`/`MeusRegistrosError` already use); drawer closes either way. The CONVERSAS + static-nav block now scrolls as one unit (`Expanded`+`SingleChildScrollView`) so a longer session list can't overflow the fixed-height `Drawer`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart` — added a `ScrollController` listener that calls `cubit.recordScrollOffset` continuously; the `BlocConsumer` listener now tracks `_lastSessionId` to distinguish "the active session just changed" from an ordinary in-session update, jumping to `restoreScrollOffset` (or the bottom, if `null`) only on the former, and requesting focus on a new `FocusNode` (`_composerFocusNode`, now threaded through `_ChatComposer`) when a session switch lands on zero messages — this satisfies AC2 ("composer focused" on a fresh "Novo Chat") without any new cubit API.
- `test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart` — new group covering: switching fetches and activates the target session; switching to the already-active session is a no-op `Right` (identical state object, no re-fetch); a switch failure surfaces as `Left` with the old session still active; `recordScrollOffset`/`restoreScrollOffset` round-trip (including the "never recorded -> null" fallback); `startNewSession` online success (new empty session, prepended to `sessions`); offline failure (state object untouched, `Left(NetworkOffline)`).
- `test/core/widgets/app_drawer_test.dart` — this file already existed (Story 1.6), asserting the *old* "no CONVERSAS section, Novo Chat is a dead no-op" behavior, so I rewrote it in place rather than creating a duplicate. It now wraps the test route in `BlocProvider<ChatCubit>.value` with a controllable fake `ChatRepository` (mirroring the pattern at `app_router_test.dart:128-156`) and covers: CONVERSAS rendering (+ "Nova conversa" fallback), tap-to-switch, no-op on the already-active row, "Novo Chat" online success, "Novo Chat" offline (untouched session + SnackBar text), plus the pre-existing header/nav/width assertions (unchanged).

## Verification

- `fvm flutter analyze` — 0 issues.
- `fvm flutter test` — all 915 tests pass (full suite, including the untouched pre-existing `chat_flow_e2e_test.dart`, `chat_screen_test.dart`, `app_router_test.dart`).
- `fvm flutter pub get` — resolves cleanly, no conflicts.
- No `build_runner` run needed — no new/changed `freezed`/`json_serializable` types.

## Two deliberate, low-risk deviations from the spec's literal wording

1. Spec/Boundaries says `switchSession`/`startNewSession` return `Future<Either<Failure, void>>`. I used `Future<Either<Failure, Unit>>` (fpdart's `Unit`) instead — using `void` as the generic `Right` type triggers Dart's `void_checks` lint (`return right(unit)` reads as "assignment to a variable of type void"), which fails AGENTS.md's hard "`flutter analyze` must report zero issues" requirement. `Either<Failure, Unit>` is also the codebase's own existing convention for this exact shape (`SessionRepository.restoreSession`, `AccountSettingsRepository.setBiometricEnabled`, `VaultRepository.authenticate`/`submitPin` all do this). Behavior is identical; only the type-parameter spelling differs.
2. The Code Map labeled `test/core/widgets/app_drawer_test.dart` "(new)" — it was not; it already existed from Story 1.6 testing the drawer's pre-session behavior. Implemented spec-6-2 (Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation) in full. Summary of changes, verification, and two deliberate deviations below.

## Files changed

- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart` — `ChatReady` gained `sessions: List<ChatSession>` and `restoreScrollOffset: double?`; `copyWith` extended to carry both.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart`
  - `_bootstrap()` now captures the resolved session list (including a freshly created one) into the emitted `ChatReady.sessions`.
  - Added `final Map<String, double> _scrollOffsets = {}` (in-memory, keyed by sessionId, lives on the long-lived cubit — never Hive, never ChatReady).
  - Added `recordScrollOffset(sessionId, offset)`.
  - Added `switchSession(sessionId) -> Future<Either<Failure, Unit>>`: no-op `Right` if already active; otherwise fetches history via the existing `listMessages`, emits a new `ChatReady` carrying whatever `_scrollOffsets[sessionId]` holds (or `null`).
  - Added `startNewSession() -> Future<Either<Failure, Unit>>`: calls existing `createSession()`; on `Left` (including offline) nothing is emitted at all — current session untouched; on success, new empty session becomes active, prepended to `sessions`.
- `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart` — rewritten to read `context.read<ChatCubit>()`/`BlocBuilder<ChatCubit, ChatState>` (the instance `ChatScreen` already provides via `BlocProvider<ChatCubit>.value`, never a second `sl<ChatCubit>()`). Added a "CONVERSAS" section (`_ConversasSection`/`_DrawerSessionItem`, reusing `drawerNavItemPadding`/`textBodyMd`/`textMonoCaption`/`spacingXs`/`spacingSm` — no new design tokens) listing every session title+timestamp, sorted most-recent-first, empty title falling back to "Nova conversa". Wired "Novo Chat" to `startNewSession()` and each row to `switchSession()`, both `await`ed with the `Left` surfaced as a `ScaffoldMessenger` `SnackBar` (`failure.message` verbatim, same convention `TextEntryError`/`MeusRegistrosError` already use); drawer closes either way. The CONVERSAS + static-nav block now scrolls as one unit (`Expanded`+`SingleChildScrollView`) so a longer session list can't overflow the fixed-height `Drawer`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart` — added a `ScrollController` listener that calls `cubit.recordScrollOffset` continuously; the `BlocConsumer` listener now tracks `_lastSessionId` to distinguish "the active session just changed" from an ordinary in-session update, jumping to `restoreScrollOffset` (or the bottom, if `null`) only on the former, and requesting focus on a new `FocusNode` (`_composerFocusNode`, now threaded through `_ChatComposer`) when a session switch lands on zero messages — this satisfies AC2 ("composer focused" on a fresh "Novo Chat") without any new cubit API.
- `test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart` — new group covering: switching fetches and activates the target session; switching to the already-active session is a no-op `Right` (identical state object, no re-fetch); a switch failure surfaces as `Left` with the old session still active; `recordScrollOffset`/`restoreScrollOffset` round-trip (including the "never recorded -> null" fallback); `startNewSession` online success (new empty session, prepended to `sessions`); offline failure (state object untouched, `Left(NetworkOffline)`).
- `test/core/widgets/app_drawer_test.dart` — this file already existed (Story 1.6), asserting the *old* "no CONVERSAS section, Novo Chat is a dead no-op" behavior, so I rewrote it in place rather than creating a duplicate. It now wraps the test route in `BlocProvider<ChatCubit>.value` with a controllable fake `ChatRepository` (mirroring the pattern at `app_router_test.dart:128-156`) and covers: CONVERSAS rendering (+ "Nova conversa" fallback), tap-to-switch, no-op on the already-active row, "Novo Chat" online success, "Novo Chat" offline (untouched session + SnackBar text), plus the pre-existing header/nav/width assertions (unchanged).

- `fvm flutter analyze` — 0 issues.
- `fvm flutter test` — all 915 tests pass (full suite, including the untouched pre-existing `chat_flow_e2e_test.dart`, `chat_screen_test.dart`, `app_router_test.dart`).
- `fvm flutter pub get` — resolves cleanly, no conflicts.
- No `build_runner` run needed — no new/changed `freezed`/`json_serializable` types.

## Two deliberate, low-risk deviations from the spec's literal wording

1. Spec/Boundaries says `switchSession`/`startNewSession` return `Future<Either<Failure, void>>`. I used `Future<Either<Failure, Unit>>` (fpdart's `Unit`) instead — using `void` as the generic `Right` type triggers Dart's `void_checks` lint (`return right(unit)` reads as "assignment to a variable of type void"), which fails AGENTS.md's hard "`flutter analyze` must report zero issues" requirement. `Either<Failure, Unit>` is also the codebase's own existing convention for this exact shape (`SessionRepository.restoreSession`, `AccountSettingsRepository.setBiometricEnabled`, `VaultRepository.authenticate`/`submitPin` all do this). Behavior is identical; only the type-parameter spelling differs.
2. The Code Map labeled `test/core/widgets/app_drawer_test.dart` "(new)" — it was not; it already existed from Story 1.6 testing the drawer's pre-session behavior. I extended/rewrote it in place instead of creating a second file, since the old assertions ("no CONVERSAS section", "Novo Chat is a no-op") are now literally false and would otherwise fail.

message.content:
The coordinator sent a message while you were working:
Code review of your spec-6-2 implementation surfaced 4 "patch" findings (trivially-fixable, confirmed real) that need fixing now. Apply all four:

1. **Cross-session stream leakage (high severity).** `ChatCubit.switchSession()` and `startNewSession()` don't cancel the in-flight `_sendSubscription` or check `_isSending` before switching the active session. If a user switches sessions (or starts a new one) while an AI response is still streaming, the orphaned subscription's `onData`/`onDone` callbacks keep firing and apply token/done events to whatever session is now active — cross-session message corruption. Fix: at the top of both `switchSession()` and `startNewSession()`, if `_isSending` is true, do the same cleanup `close()` already does — cancel `_sendSubscription`, complete+null `_sendCompleter` if pending, reset `_isSending = false` — before proceeding with the switch/create. Add a regression test in `chat_cubit_test.dart` that starts a send (don't let the fake stream complete), then calls `switchSession`/`startNewSession`, and asserts the old stream's late-arriving events never mutate the new active session's state.

2. **Crash risk in the new `_ConversasSection` sort.** `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart`'s new `_ConversasSection` sorts sessions via `DateTime.parse(b.updatedAt).compareTo(DateTime.parse(a.updatedAt))` — an uncaught `FormatException` on a malformed `updatedAt` crashes the whole drawer build. Fix: use the same crash-safe pattern already sitting right next to it in the same file (`_formatSessionTimestamp`'s `DateTime.tryParse(...)` fallback) — e.g. `(DateTime.tryParse(b.updatedAt) ?? DateTime(0)).compareTo(DateTime.tryParse(a.updatedAt) ?? DateTime(0))`. Add a widget test with a session carrying a malformed `updatedAt` string, asserting the drawer still renders instead of throwing.

3. **Zero screen-level test coverage for 2 of this story's 4 acceptance criteria.** `ChatScreen`'s own `_lastSessionId`/`_jumpToOffset`/`_focusComposerSoon` wiring — the actual implementation of "new session opens with composer focused" and "returning session restores scroll position" — is never exercised by any test that pumps the real `ChatScreen` through a session switch. Existing tests only check `ChatCubit`'s state field directly (`chat_cubit_test.dart`) or drive `AppDrawer` against a bare `Scaffold` with no real `ChatScreen` underneath (`app_drawer_test.dart`). Fix: add a case (or two) to `test/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen_test.dart` that drives a real `switchSession`/`startNewSession` through a pumped `ChatScreen` (via a fake repository with 2+ sessions) and asserts (a) the composer's `FocusNode` gains focus when a new empty session becomes active, and (b) `_scrollController`'s position reflects a previously recorded offset when switching back to a session that had one.

4. **Inaccurate doc comment.** `ChatScreen`'s `_focusComposerSoon()` doc comment claims it's "only ever called right after a *new* session ... becomes active with no messages yet, never on an ordinary switch to a past (non-empty) session" — but the actual guard is just `state.messages.isEmpty`, so switching to any past session that happens to be empty also triggers it. The behavior is fine (focusing composer on an empty past session isn't wrong), only the comment overclaims. Fix: reword the comment to describe the actual guard (`messages.isEmpty`) rather than claiming it's exclusive to brand-new sessions.

After applying all four: re-run `fvm flutter analyze` (zero issues) and `fvm flutter test` (all pass, including your new regression tests), then report back what changed and the verification output.

Address this before completing your current task.

content.text:
All four review findings have been fixed and verified. Here's what changed:

**1. Cross-session stream leakage (high severity) — fixed in `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart`**
Added `_cancelInFlightSend()`, mirroring `close()`'s existing cleanup exactly (cancel `_sendSubscription`, complete+null `_sendCompleter` if pending, reset `_isSending`). Called at the top of `switchSession()` (after the same-session no-op check — a true no-op reload must never kill its own legitimately-streaming response) and unconditionally at the top of `startNewSession()`. Added two regression tests in `chat_cubit_test.dart`; I confirmed both genuinely fail (timeout) when the `_cancelInFlightSend()` calls are removed, and pass with the fix.

**2. Crash risk in `_ConversasSection`'s sort — fixed in `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart`**
Replaced `DateTime.parse` with the crash-safe `DateTime.tryParse(...) ?? DateTime(0)` pattern already used by `_formatSessionTimestamp` next to it. Added a widget test with a malformed `updatedAt`; confirmed it fails with a `FormatException` when reverted to `DateTime.parse`, passes with the fix.

**Adjacent fix found while verifying #2:** `ChatCubit._bootstrap`'s own "reuse the most recent" sort (pre-existing, from story 6.1 — not one of the four, and not touched by spec-6-2) has the identical `DateTime.parse` crash risk, and it crashes *before* ever reaching the drawer's code — it blocked me from even exercising fix #2 with a realistic multi-session scenario. I applied the same one-line `tryParse` fix there too. Flagging this explicitly since it's outside the four named items, though it's the same pattern, same fix, essentially zero risk, and otherwise leaves the app crashing on real malformed session data.

**3. Missing screen-level coverage for AC2/AC4 — added to `test/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen_test.dart`**
Added two tests driving a real pumped `ChatScreen`: one confirms the composer's `FocusNode` gains focus when `startNewSession()` lands on an empty session (isolated from the initial-bootstrap case by giving the initial session non-empty history first); the other confirms `ListView`'s `ScrollController.position.pixels` is restored to a previously-recorded offset when switching back to a session, rather than jumping to the bottom. Extended that file's `_FakeChatRepository` with a settable `createSessionResult`. I confirmed both tests fail when I temporarily disabled the corresponding `chat_screen.dart` logic, and pass with it intact.

**4. Inaccurate doc comment — fixed in `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart`**
Reworded `_focusComposerSoon`'s comment to state the actual guard (`state.messages.isEmpty`) and explicitly note it also fires on an empty past session, rather than claiming exclusivity to brand-new sessions.

**Verification:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` — 0 issues.
- `fvm flutter test` — all 920 tests pass (915 previously + 5 new: 2 in `chat_cubit_test.dart`, 1 in `app_drawer_test.dart`, 2 in `chat_screen_test.dart`).
- Each of the 4 new/modified regression tests was individually verified to fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the post-fix code (by temporarily reverting each fix, confirming the test catches it, then restoring).
